newsitem.title: USA: Western Auto closes 69 stores, 1600 jobs lost.
newsitem.headline: Western Auto closes 69 stores, 1600 jobs lost.

text.p: Western Auto Supply Co said Tuesday it closed 69 of its stores in 19 markets yesterday as it accelerates its plan to convert its auto repair operations into Parts America stores, which only sell auto parts.
The closings eliminate 1,600 jobs, including about 1,100 store employees and about 400 people involved in Western Auto's private trucking fleet.

Sears, Roebuck and Co, parent of Kansas City, Mo.-based Western Auto, will be taking a non-material charge in the 1997 third quarter to cover costs of the closings, a Western Auto spokesman told Reuters. The amount of the charge is not available at this time, he said.
Western Auto employees were informed of the closings yesterday. The employees will be offered jobs in other Sears businesses and receive outplacement services.
Western Auto, which had 279 stores before yesterday's closings, expects to complete conversion of the remaining 210 stores to the Parts America format by year end, he said.
The decision to accelerate the conversion process was based on strong performance of stores already converted.

"Our new Parts America stores are performing well, and we feel compelled to speed up our schedule and get all our stores converted by the end of the year," said Donald Shaffer, chairman and chief executive officer of Western Auto, in a news release.
The stores that were closed could not be converted successfully into parts-only stores, he said.

Western Auto also said it plans to open 100 new Parts America stores in 1997 and 150 in 1998. The company said it is on track to achieve its goal of operating more than 1,000 Parts America stores by the end of 1999.
In another development, Western Auto said it will outsource its trucking operations to Schneider National, based in Green Bay, Wis.

Western Auto, which was bought by Sears in 1988, operates 392 Parts America stores, 279 Western Auto. In addition, there are 820 Western Auto independently owned and operated stores in the U.S., which are not affected by the conversions to Parts America.
